title: introduce-cost-sentinel-prefetch-catalog-and-quant-tier-optimizer
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Adds a tenant-level prefetch coalescer (Cost Sentinel) and a conservative quantization-tier selector with CLI tooling. Backwards-compatible; new feature gated behind feature flag 'cost_sentinel_v1'.
description: Context: Customers with mixed bursty and steady traffic were seeing suboptimal unit economics from 'eager' prefetch defaults and a single global quantization policy. This change introduces a cost-aware prefetch coalescer (Cost Sentinel) that builds a lightweight tenant prefetch catalog and a Quant Tier Optimizer that selects conservative quant profiles at rollout time. Motivation: reduce per-token cost on mid-size tenants while preserving latency SLOs and preventing quality regressions during quant rollouts. Key changes: 1) server/prefetch/cost_sentinel.py — new coalescer that synthesizes tenant prefetch catalogs from short-window request traces, implements an eviction heuristic (LRU by last-use + size score) and exposes a bounded catalog API; 2) service/econ/quant_selector.go — runtime policy to map tenant catalogs + workload shape to a quant tier (fp16 / int8-safe / int8-aggressive) with safety gates based on eval-set regressions and token loss thresholds; 3) cli/econ-inspect/main.go — developer CLI to inspect tenant prefetch catalog, simulate cost delta for candidate quant tiers, and produce a dry-run report; 4) docs/operator/prefetch.md — operational guidance on feature flagging, rollout windows, and recommended observation queries; 5) tests/e2e/prefetch_cost_test.py and unit tests for quant stability. Rollout plan: feature flag default off; enable on a small cohort (10 tenants) with shadow-prefetch mode for 48h, then canary with 1% traffic shift; automatic rollback if token-loss delta > 0.6% or latency P99 increases by >10ms. Related: closes ENG-3456 (prefetch defaults), references SUP-4123 (customer incident with cold-prefetch thrash).

review_thread: Diego Morales (2024-11-06): Nice design. A couple of questions: 1) how do we bound memory usage of tenant catalogs when there are many low-volume tenants? 2) can the quant_selector depend on offline evals only, or do we allow lightweight online probes?

Author (Samira) (2024-11-06): Catalogs are bounded per-tenant (default 128 entries) and overall memory is protected by a global low-memory eviction path that compacts cold tenants every 5m (configurable). Quant selector supports both offline eval-set checks and an online 'probe' mode gated behind a tenant opt-in and the feature flag — added to docs.

Ava Chen (2024-11-08): Tests look good. Suggestion: make the default safety threshold more conservative (token-loss delta 0.6% -> 0.4%) for the initial canary. Also add an alert playbook entry for false-positive regressions.
Author (Samira) (2024-11-09): Lowered default to 0.4% and added alert playbook snippet to docs. Addressed minor nits in CLI help text.
Liam O'Connor (2024-11-11): CI flaked once due to lint rule; reran and green. Approving — please squash when merging.

observability_notes: Adds two new metrics: prefetch_catalog_entries{tenant} and quant_selection_decision{tenant,tier}. Dashboards: operator/prefetch-cost -> new panels for catalog growth, simulated cost delta, and quant stability scores.
operational_playbook: Enable feature flag 'cost_sentinel_v1' set to 'shadow' first. Monitor quant_selection_decision for 'int8-aggressive' picks; if token_loss_delta > 0.4% or p99 latency delta > +10ms, flip to rollback. For hotfix: set feature flag to 'off' and run 'cli/econ-inspect simulate --tenant <id> --rollback' to verify revert behavior.
notes_for_release_manager: Gate behind 'cost_sentinel_v1' feature flag. Recommend A/B rollout: shadow 10 tenants -> canary 1% traffic -> ramp 10% -> full. Telemetry retention for new metrics should be at least 7d during rollout. Inform SRE and Solutions Eng teams to prep playbook and customer-facing notes.
